It always increases the optimum, since options add behaviours

questions.prompt: Which log would best reveal option collapse in a learned hierarchy?
options: Gradient norm of the encoder per update
Learning-rate schedule of the high-level optimiser
Training loss of the critic over time
Histogram of option usage and mean option duration
questions.explanation: One option used everywhere or durations of 1 indicate collapse.

questions.prompt: Which is a legitimate reason to prefer hand-designed options over learned ones?
options: The sub-skills are known and must be safe and testable
Learned options need no reward signal to be trained
Hand-designed options remove the need for a termination condition
Learned options never collapse onto a single option
questions.explanation: Known decomposition + testability favour hand design.

questions.prompt: A navigation option starts in a room whose door is closed. The initiation set should:
options: Be ignored, because the termination beta handles it
Exclude that state, since the skill cannot succeed there
Be empty, so the option is never started
Include it, since failure teaches the high level
questions.explanation: An initiation set is the precondition; including states where the skill is invalid creates avoidable failures.

questions.prompt: Corridor of length 20 (goal at 20, reward -1, primitives only). Starting from V=-100 (goal 0), how many synchronous sweeps until the value reaches state 0 for the first time?
questions.explanation: One state per sweep: goal-adjacent state in sweep 1 ... state 0 in sweep 20.
